headline: AI-driven record highs coexist with a hawkish Fed and oil shock
body: Equity markets keep grinding to fresh highs even as the macro backdrop turns tougher underneath them. The Nasdaq closed at a record after another AI-led session, with infrastructure names extending gains on optimism around Meta's newly unveiled Muse AI agent, while the Dow lagged and premarket futures were essentially flat heading into Wednesday. That divergence is playing out against a Fed that just delivered its first hike since 2023, lifting rates to 3.75%-4% on persistent inflation from tariffs, energy costs, and AI-driven capital spending, with markets now pricing further hikes at both remaining 2026 meetings. Treasury yields and mortgage rates have climbed in response, yet the VIX sits in the mid-teens — a level that reads more complacent than cautious given how much is now in motion.

Thursday's Trump-Xi summit in Washington looks like the real swing factor for the rest of the week: trade-truce extensions, rare-earth export predictability, and AI-governance friction are all on the table, and semiconductor and Asian tech names have already firmed into the meeting on hopes for a constructive outcome. Oil remains the other wildcard, with WTI still holding near $100 after Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic collapsed amid the ongoing Iran conflict, a supply shock that keeps headline inflation sticky and narrows the Fed's room to maneuver. Retail-sentiment chatter was thin and non-specific in today's search, so this read leans more on price action, Fed positioning, and geopolitical headlines than on any clear social-media consensus about direction.
